tweets.text:
The market can stay boring for much longer than most traders can stay patient.

That’s usually where accounts get chipped away. Not in the volatile periods, but in the quiet ones.

Risk management is especially important because it can be easy to size up because volatility is low, only to take a lot of unnecessary losses in doing so.

Demand for privacy and security grows every day. Across the world, and especially in crypto.

$AF lets you send crypto to a @ name, and every transfer lands on a one-time stealth address that only the sender and receiver can see.

They’re also adding quantum-resistant signing that protects your wallet without requiring a new address.

Privacy and quantum security in one project. Two narratives the market keeps coming back which makes it interesting to me. I’ve invested in @Americanfort_io. Launching soon.

quote.text:
Our CEO @MehowHacks spoke to @Forbes on what the $6.3B Binance hack means for banks heading into stablecoin issuance under the GENIUS Act.

The short version: the attackers didn’t break code. They compromised three people.

At a bank there are no cryptographic proofs at all, only more people in the way. The fix isn’t more approvals but a system where withdrawals can’t happen unless the user authorises them, and nobody can withdraw what they can’t prove they deposited.

That’s what we’ve built. Full piece ↓

tweets.text:
$BTC Is about to close its 5th consecutive weekly candle in the red.

The last time we hit 5+ was this February when it topped at 6.

The only other time before that was all the way in 2022 when we saw 9 consecutive red weekly candles.

So to see 5 in a row is quite a rare sighting. The other two streaks happened in middle of a bear market and when price traded below the bull market support band in a bearish structure.

Next week is going to be interesting as I suspect we will get a resolution on this either way. Eyes on the weekly closes.
